# Opus Custom reference vectors

The `custom*` directories contain independent outputs from Opus revision
`503d81b138d76621aae4b12786e90de48aa8db3a`, built with `CUSTOM_MODES` and
`ENABLE_OPUS_CUSTOM_API`. The fixed directory additionally uses `FIXED_POINT`.
The `fixed24` profile additionally enables `ENABLE_RES24`; `-pfa` profiles
enable `ENABLE_PFA`. All builds disable floating-point contraction and fast math.

Regenerate from the repository root:

```sh
sh tools/reference/build_custom.sh float
python3 tools/reference/generate_custom_vectors.py float
sh tools/reference/build_custom.sh fixed
python3 tools/reference/generate_custom_vectors.py fixed
sh tools/reference/build_custom.sh fixed24
python3 tools/reference/generate_custom_vectors.py fixed24
# Repeat the two commands for float-pfa, fixed-pfa and fixed24-pfa.
```

`cases.txt` lists sample rates and frame sizes. The modes include 8, 12, 16,
22.05, 32, 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz, canonical modes and nonstandard transform sizes.
The 90-sample case checks an 88-sample overlap whose fixed-point window must be
rounded directly from double precision.

Each `.mode` file contains the mode dimensions, band boundaries, logarithmic
band widths, window, preemphasis coefficients and allocation vectors. Float
coefficients are hexadecimal IEEE-754 bits; fixed coefficients are integers
with the Q formats used by C.

Each `.tsv` file has three encoded frames followed by two concealed lost
frames, for one or two channels. Columns are the operation marker, frame
index, packet size, encoder final range, decoder final range, packet bytes
(`-` for loss), little-endian 16-bit PCM, float output bits and signed 24-bit
output represented as eight hexadecimal digits per sample. The encoder uses
complexity 10 and an 80-byte packet buffer. Inputs use the deterministic ramp
defined in `tools/reference/custom_oracle.c`.

The Rust test compares packets, final ranges and all three decoder output
formats exactly; expected values are never generated by Rust.
The additional `-24.tsv` streams at 32 kHz stereo, 48 kHz/90 samples and
96 kHz/960 samples contain fractional 16-bit sample values, exercising the
24-bit and float input APIs. In total each profile contains 33 streams and
165 normal or concealed frames. Reset checks replay each standard stream's
first C frame after resetting the codec state.

`custom/constructors.txt` records 8,302 C constructor outcomes across 14 rates
and sizes from 0 through 1,030. Unsupported FFT factorizations are excluded
from this C sweep: the pinned C allocation-failure cleanup can double-free
these cases. Separate Rust checks require those sizes to return an error
without a panic. The Rust implementation does not reproduce that C memory bug.

QEXT profiles append `-qext` before the optional `-pfa` suffix in both build
and generation commands, for example `float-qext-pfa` or `fixed24-qext`.
Each adds 96 kHz frames of 240, 480, 1440, 1920 and 2048 samples, plus the
48 kHz/720-sample mode. Before the explicit extension cases below, each QEXT
profile contains 43 streams and 215 normal or concealed frames. `custom-float-qext/constructors.txt` repeats the
constructor sweep under QEXT's different mode rules (8,260 outcomes).
Unsupported dimensions above 1024 also receive Rust rejection checks; the C sweep remains capped at
1030 because later C allocation-failure paths can double-free mode storage.

The QEXT `mode-cases.txt` additionally includes the valid 96 kHz/2048-sample
mode. Only its table and constructor results are recorded: the pinned C
normal decoder can read before its prediction-history allocation for that
mode. Rust rejects creating the affected decoder; undefined C memory reads
are not compatibility goldens.

Eight `-ext.tsv` streams per QEXT profile enable `OPUS_SET_QEXT(1)` and use
800-byte packets, covering both channel counts at 48 kHz/720 and 960 samples
and 96 kHz/1440 and 1920 samples. They exercise the public extension control,
actual extension payloads, and subsequent loss concealment. Including these
streams, each QEXT profile has 51 streams and 255 frames. Mode fixtures also
record extension band boundaries, C's log-width table, and all three pulse
cache arrays (`QB`, `QL`, `QI`, `QT`, `QC`).
